Working in Orleans

Where the Cape takes the weather.

Orleans sits where the Cape turns north, with Cape Cod Bay at Rock Harbor on one side and the Atlantic at Nauset on the other. Homes in East Orleans and around Pleasant Bay take wind-driven rain and salt straight off the ocean, and it shows first on the east and north walls.

The houses are mostly cedar-shingled capes, half-capes and shingle-style homes, many of them second homes. Typical work here is trim that has opened up at the corners, shingles that have cupped or split, deck boards and railings worn by salt air, and windows that let water in at the head.

On exposed elevations we often suggest PVC or cellular trim instead of wood, and stainless or coated fasteners. We'll walk you through the trade-offs in look and cost.

What we check first on Orleans homes

  • East- and north-facing walls: trim joints, shingles, window heads
  • Deck railings and fasteners exposed to salt air
  • Corner boards and rake trim on shingle-style homes
  • Sliding doors and sills facing the water

Historic review on 6A

Orleans is part of the Old King's Highway Regional Historic District. Visible exterior changes in the district may need approval before work starts. We'll check at the estimate.

FAQ

Orleans questions, answered.

Do you work in East Orleans and South Orleans?

Yes, all of Orleans, including the village, East Orleans and South Orleans.

What trim holds up best near Nauset or Pleasant Bay?

On exposed walls we often recommend PVC or cellular trim with stainless or coated fasteners. Wood still works where it's protected. We'll go through options at the estimate.

I don't live in Orleans year-round. Can you still do the work?

Yes. We agree the scope and price in writing and keep you updated with photos, so you don't need to be on site.

Do you replace cedar shingles or only repair them?

Both. Sometimes a few courses are enough. When the wall has reached its limit, we re-shingle with proper flashing at every window and corner.
